notInObjectives: AZ-305 tests design decisions. Step-by-step administration (AZ-104 territory) appears only where a design depends on it.
Earning Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert also requires the Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) certification.
Azure Active Directory is now Microsoft Entra ID; Azure AD B2C new sign-ups have moved to Microsoft Entra External ID. Questions use current names.
The Log Analytics agent (MMA) was retired in August 2024; designs use the Azure Monitor Agent with data collection rules.
Azure Cache for Redis is being replaced by Azure Managed Redis for new designs; questions name both where relevant.
Azure Stack HCI is now Azure Local.

vCore-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB is now Azure DocumentDB. Synapse Link for Cosmos DB isn't offered for new projects (Fabric mirroring replaces it), and Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is retiring in favour of Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters.
Azure Blueprints is deprecated; designs use template specs and deployment stacks.

Retired migration tools: Azure Data Studio and its SQL migration extension (February 2026) and Data Migration Assistant (July 2025). Current options are Azure DMS in the portal or CLI, the Arc-enabled SQL Server migration experience, and Azure Migrate. Data Box Heavy is retired; next-generation Data Box replaces it.
Azure SQL Edge and Azure Database for MariaDB are retired.

sessions.title: Logging design: workspaces, diagnostic settings and log routing
sessions.scope: Log Analytics workspace design (single vs multiple, region, access modes, retention and archive, table plans: Analytics/Basic/Auxiliary at concept level, cost), Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules, diagnostic settings, activity log, resource logs, routing to Log Analytics / Storage / Event Hubs / partner solutions, sending logs to a SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel as a destination, log retention and compliance, cross-tenant/cross-subscription logging.

sessions.title: Monitoring design: Azure Monitor, Application Insights, alerts and insights
sessions.scope: Azure Monitor metrics vs logs, Application Insights (workspace-based, distributed tracing, availability tests), VM insights, Container insights, Network Watcher (connection monitor, flow logs), alerts and action groups, alert processing rules, workbooks and dashboards, Azure Managed Grafana, Service Health and Resource Health alerts, Azure Advisor, Defender for Cloud monitoring, choosing monitoring for hybrid via Azure Arc.

sessions.title: Authentication and identity management design
sessions.scope: Microsoft Entra ID tenants, hybrid identity (Entra Connect Sync vs Cloud Sync; password hash sync, pass-through authentication, federation with AD FS — trade-offs), seamless SSO, MFA and authentication strengths, passwordless (Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 passkeys, Authenticator), Conditional Access design, Identity Protection risk policies, external identities (B2B collaboration, B2B direct connect, Entra External ID for customers), multitenant apps, app registrations vs enterprise apps, managed identities (system vs user-assigned) as workload identity, workload identity federation.

sessions.title: Authorizing access to Azure and on-premises resources
sessions.scope: Azure RBAC design (built-in vs custom roles, scope selection, least privilege, deny assignments at concept level, role assignment limits), Microsoft Entra roles vs Azure roles, Privileged Identity Management for just-in-time access, Azure Lighthouse for cross-tenant management, attribute-based access control conditions for storage, data-plane vs control-plane authorization (Key Vault RBAC, Storage data roles, Cosmos DB RBAC), shared access signatures vs Entra authorization; on-premises: Microsoft Entra application proxy / Private Access, Entra Domain Services, Kerberos constrained delegation, hybrid access to on-prem apps, Azure Arc for on-prem servers with RBAC.

sessions.title: Secrets, certificates and keys: Key Vault and Managed HSM
sessions.scope: Azure Key Vault (vaults vs Managed HSM, Standard vs Premium SKU, FIPS levels at concept level), secrets/keys/certificates, access model (Azure RBAC recommended vs access policies), soft delete and purge protection, key rotation and expiry, certificate auto-renewal with integrated CAs, Key Vault references in App Service/Functions and App Configuration, customer-managed keys for storage/SQL TDE/disk encryption, double encryption, private endpoints and firewall for Key Vault, one vault per app per environment per region guidance, managed identities to access Key Vault, Dedicated HSM/Cloud HSM at mention level.

sessions.title: Governance structure: management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and tagging
sessions.scope: Management group hierarchy design (depth limits, keep it shallow, platform vs landing zones, sandbox, decommissioned), Azure landing zones (Cloud Adoption Framework), subscription design as unit of scale/billing/policy, subscription limits and quotas, subscription vending, resource group design by lifecycle, naming conventions, tagging strategy (mandatory tags, enforcement and inheritance with Azure Policy, cost allocation), Enterprise Agreement / MCA billing hierarchy at concept level, Azure Policy and RBAC assignment at the right scope.

sessions.title: Compliance and identity governance
sessions.scope: Compliance: Azure Policy initiatives and regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud, Microsoft cloud security benchmark, policy effects for remediation, Microsoft Purview (data map, classification, Compliance Manager), resource locks, Azure Blueprints deprecation in favour of template specs/deployment stacks, audit logging, data residency; Identity governance: Privileged Identity Management, access reviews, entitlement management and access packages, lifecycle workflows, Conditional Access governance, guest user lifecycle, emergency access accounts, separation of duties.

sessions.title: Relational data: choosing the right SQL and open-source database service
sessions.scope: Azure SQL Database (single, elastic pool), Azure SQL Managed Instance (instance-level features: SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR, Service Broker, near 100% compatibility), SQL Server on Azure VMs (full control, OS access, unsupported features), Azure Database for PostgreSQL / MySQL flexible server, choosing by compatibility, management effort, features, cost and licensing (Azure Hybrid Benefit), Azure SQL Edge at mention level.

sessions.title: SQL tiers, scalability and data protection
sessions.scope: Purchasing models DTU vs vCore, service tiers General Purpose / Business Critical / Hyperscale, serverless compute tier with auto-pause, provisioned compute, elastic pools for many databases with variable load, scaling up/down, read scale-out replicas, Hyperscale named replicas, sharding with elastic database tools, partitioning; data protection: TDE (service- vs customer-managed key), Always Encrypted (with secure enclaves), dynamic data masking, row-level security, auditing, Defender for SQL, Microsoft Entra authentication, private endpoints, ledger tables.

sessions.title: Semi-structured data: Azure Cosmos DB and Table storage
sessions.scope: Azure Cosmos DB APIs (NoSQL, MongoDB vCore vs RU, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table, PostgreSQL), consistency levels (strong, bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix, eventual) and trade-offs, partition key design, request units, provisioned vs autoscale vs serverless throughput, multi-region writes, TTL, change feed, analytical store / Synapse Link at concept level, Azure Table Storage vs Cosmos DB for Table, JSON documents in SQL, choosing for global low-latency apps.

sessions.title: Unstructured data: Blob, Data Lake and Files — cost, performance and durability
sessions.scope: Blob Storage vs Azure Data Lake Storage (hierarchical namespace) vs Azure Files vs Azure NetApp Files vs Managed Disks; standard vs premium performance; access tiers Hot/Cool/Cold/Archive and lifecycle management; reserved capacity; redundancy LRS/ZRS/GRS/GZRS/RA-; protection: soft delete for blobs and containers, versioning, point-in-time restore, immutable storage (time-based and legal hold), object replication, encryption with CMK, private endpoints, SAS strategy, Defender for Storage; cost/performance balancing scenarios.

sessions.title: Data integration and analysis
sessions.scope: Azure Data Factory (pipelines, copy activity, mapping data flows, integration runtimes: Azure, self-hosted, Azure-SSIS), Microsoft Fabric (OneLake, Data Factory in Fabric, lakehouse, warehouse) at design level, Azure Synapse Analytics (dedicated vs serverless SQL pools, Spark), Azure Databricks, Azure Stream Analytics and Event Hubs for streaming, Azure Data Explorer for log/telemetry analytics, Power BI at mention level, medallion architecture, batch vs real-time, choosing ETL vs ELT.

sessions.title: Disaster recovery design: RPO, RTO and Azure Site Recovery
sessions.scope: RPO and RTO definitions and how to derive them, availability vs recoverability, DR strategies (backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active) and their cost, Azure Site Recovery for Azure-to-Azure, VMware/physical and Hyper-V to Azure (recovery plans, test failover, failback, replication policy, crash- vs app-consistent recovery points), region pairs and non-paired regions, hybrid DR, DR for PaaS (geo-replication), DR drills, Azure Business Continuity Center.

sessions.title: Backup design for compute, databases and unstructured data
sessions.scope: Azure Backup: Recovery Services vault vs Backup vault, backup policies and retention, VM backup (standard vs enhanced policy, instant restore, file-level restore, cross-region restore), MARS agent, MABS/DPM for on-prem, immutable vaults, soft delete, multi-user authorization; databases: Azure SQL automated backups with point-in-time restore and long-term retention, geo-restore, SQL Server in Azure VM backup, PostgreSQL/MySQL backups, Cosmos DB periodic vs continuous backup; unstructured: operational vs vaulted blob backup, Azure Files share snapshots and backup, ADLS considerations.

sessions.title: High availability for compute
sessions.scope: Availability sets vs availability zones vs Virtual Machine Scale Sets (flexible orchestration), zone-redundant vs zonal deployments, VM SLAs, App Service zone redundancy and multi-region, AKS availability zones and node pools, Azure Functions Premium zone redundancy, Container Apps zone redundancy, load balancing with Azure Load Balancer (zone-redundant frontends) and Application Gateway v2, multi-region active-active with Azure Front Door or Traffic Manager, health probes, stateless design, proximity placement groups trade-off, composite SLA calculations.

sessions.title: High availability for relational, semi-structured and unstructured data
sessions.scope: Azure SQL Database zone redundancy, active geo-replication vs auto-failover groups (listener endpoints, read-only endpoint), Business Critical local replicas, Hyperscale HA replicas, SQL Managed Instance failover groups, SQL Server on VMs Always On availability groups and failover cluster instances, PostgreSQL/MySQL flexible server zone-redundant HA and read replicas; Cosmos DB multi-region reads/writes, service-managed failover, conflict resolution, availability SLAs by configuration; storage ZRS/GZRS/RA-GZRS, customer-managed failover, last sync time, Azure Files redundancy, NetApp cross-region replication.

sessions.title: Compute design: VM-based solutions and batch processing
sessions.scope: Specifying compute components from requirements (CPU/memory/GPU, VM families, managed disk types Premium SSD v2/Ultra/Standard, ephemeral OS disks), VM Scale Sets, Azure Dedicated Host, Spot VMs, reservations and savings plans for compute, Azure Virtual Desktop as a VM-based solution, Azure VMware Solution, confidential VMs, trusted launch, Azure Compute Gallery images, VM Applications, Azure Batch (pools, jobs, tasks, low-priority/Spot nodes, auto-pool), HPC choices, choosing between Batch, AKS jobs, Functions and Container Apps jobs for batch.

sessions.title: Containers and serverless design
sessions.scope: AKS (system vs user node pools, cluster autoscaler, Azure CNI vs overlay at concept level, workload identity, private clusters, AKS Automatic), Azure Container Apps (Dapr, KEDA scaling, scale to zero, revisions, jobs, workload profiles), Azure Container Instances (burst, sidecar-free simple tasks, virtual nodes), Azure Red Hat OpenShift at mention level, Azure Container Registry (geo-replication, tasks), Azure App Service (plans, slots, containers), Azure Functions hosting plans (Flex Consumption, Premium, Dedicated) and Durable Functions patterns, Logic Apps Standard vs Consumption, choosing between them by control, scale, cost and operations.

sessions.title: Messaging and event-driven architecture
sessions.scope: Azure Service Bus (queues vs topics/subscriptions, sessions for FIFO, duplicate detection, dead-lettering, transactions, Premium tier and geo-disaster recovery/geo-replication), Azure Queue Storage (simple, large backlog), Azure Event Grid (discrete events, push, system topics, custom topics, namespaces with MQTT and pull delivery), Azure Event Hubs (streaming telemetry, partitions, consumer groups, capture, Kafka endpoint), choosing commands vs events vs streams, competing consumers, publish-subscribe, event sourcing and CQRS at concept level, IoT Hub at mention level, reliable delivery and idempotency.

sessions.title: API integration, caching, configuration and automated deployment
sessions.scope: Azure API Management (tiers incl. Consumption and v2 tiers, policies, rate limiting, products and subscriptions, self-hosted gateway, developer portal, versioning and revisions, backend for AI/OpenAI at mention level), caching: Azure Managed Redis / Azure Cache for Redis (cache-aside, session state, tiers), Azure Front Door and CDN caching, API Management response caching; configuration: Azure App Configuration (feature flags, labels, Key Vault references, snapshots), Key Vault for secrets; automated deployment: Bicep/ARM templates, Terraform, template specs, deployment stacks, GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines, deployment slots and blue-green/canary, Azure Deployment Environments at mention level.

sessions.title: Migration design: Cloud Adoption Framework, assessment and IaaS/PaaS migration
sessions.scope: Cloud Adoption Framework phases (strategy, plan, ready, adopt — migrate/modernize, govern, secure, manage), the 5 Rs / migration strategies (retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, rearchitect, rebuild, replace), Azure Migrate (discovery and assessment, dependency analysis agentless vs agent-based, business case, Azure readiness, right-sizing performance-based vs as-is), migrating servers to Azure VMs, App Service migration assistant, migrating to AKS/Container Apps, Azure VMware Solution as a migration path, wave planning, landing zone readiness, Azure Migrate appliance.

sessions.title: Database and unstructured data migration
sessions.scope: Database migration: Azure Database Migration Service (online vs offline), Azure SQL migration extension for Azure Data Studio, Data Migration Assistant for assessment, SQL Managed Instance link, log replay service, transactional replication, backup and restore to MI/VM, migrating PostgreSQL/MySQL, MongoDB to Cosmos DB, choosing target by compatibility; unstructured data: AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer, Azure Storage Mover, Azure File Sync, Azure Data Box family (Data Box, Data Box Disk, Data Box Heavy) for offline transfer, Data Factory copy for data movement, bandwidth/time calculations to choose online vs offline.

sessions.title: Network connectivity and performance design
sessions.scope: Internet connectivity: public IPs (Standard SKU, zone-redundant), NAT gateway for outbound SNAT, Azure Front Door for global ingress, private vs public endpoints, service endpoints vs Private Link, Azure DNS and Private DNS zones, DNS Private Resolver; on-premises: site-to-site VPN (active-active, zone-redundant gateways), point-to-site, ExpressRoute (circuits, peering, Global Reach, FastPath, ExpressRoute Direct, redundancy with VPN backup), Virtual WAN vs hub-and-spoke, VNet peering (global, gateway transit), route tables and user-defined routes; performance: accelerated networking, proximity placement groups, ExpressRoute for predictable latency, CDN/Front Door, Network Watcher diagnostics.

sessions.title: Network security and load balancing/routing design
sessions.scope: Network security: NSGs and application security groups, Azure Firewall (Standard vs Premium: TLS inspection, IDPS; Basic), Azure Firewall Manager and policies, forced tunnelling, Web Application Firewall on Application Gateway vs Front Door, DDoS Network Protection vs IP Protection, Azure Bastion, just-in-time VM access, private endpoints and disabling public access, network segmentation in hub-and-spoke, Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules; load balancing and routing: Azure Load Balancer (L4, regional/global/cross-region), Application Gateway (L7, path-based routing, SSL termination, autoscale), Azure Front Door (global L7, Standard vs Premium), Traffic Manager (DNS-based routing methods: priority, weighted, performance, geographic), choosing with the load-balancing decision tree.
